title: Day 50 · Week 7, Day 1 — Brain: three bubbles become five — the hemispheres bud, the cerebellum starts a three-year build, the first cortex is ten days away, and the one brain nutrient we hadn't covered
summary: The fourth Brain episode, on the last day of the thalidomide limb window. Your baby is 8–11 mm at the turn from Carnegie stage 15 to 16 (NHS: a grape, with a forehead; about 100 new brain cells a minute). O'Rahilly & Müller's 192-embryo series: the five chief brain subdivisions are recognisable this week — hemispheres budding from the telencephalon, thalamus and hypothalamus, midbrain, pons-and-cerebellum, medulla — and the cortical plate does not appear until stage 21 (~Day 63). The cerebellum's four-step, three-year build (ten Donkelaar 2003), why it is the structure most damaged by prematurity (Volpe 2009), and its 34-fold growth in the second half of pregnancy alone (Andescavage 2017, 166 fetuses). The growth curve: ~350–400 g at birth, quadrupling by three (Dekaban 1978, 4,736 brains); 86 billion neurons counted, not 100 billion, with 19% in the cortex and ~80% in the cerebellum (Azevedo 2009); 100 a minute now against ~250,000 a minute averaged over gestation (Cowan 1979). Rakic's radial units and the extra rounds of division that separate a mouse cortex from a human one; synaptogenesis before 27 weeks, peaks at 3 and 15 months, pruning into adolescence (Huttenlocher 1997); the Harvard Center's million connections a second after birth. Then what her blood carries to it this week — not much blood, by design — and the nutrient the show hadn't covered: iron. Georgieff 2020; 35.5% of pregnant women anaemic worldwide (WHO 2023); US iron deficiency 7% → 14% → 30% by trimester (Mei 2011); cord ferritin and five-year outcomes in 278 children (Tamura 2002); 532,232 Swedish children, early maternal anaemia and autism OR 1.44, ADHD 1.37, intellectual disability 2.20, holding within families (Wiegersma 2019); 44 trials, 43,274 women, anaemia at term −70% (Cochrane 2015); ACOG PB 233's first-visit blood count. And the father's one finished contribution: ~2 new mutations per year of paternal age (Kong 2012), autism RR 1.66 for fathers ≥50 in 5.77 million children (Sandin 2016), schizophrenia doubled over 45 (Malaspina 2001) — real, modest, and nothing to do.
action: Ten minutes tonight, two things. One: add question ten to the Day 40 sheet — is a full blood count in today's bloods, can a ferritin go with it, and what are her two numbers (not just 'normal')? Write them in the pregnancy file with the date when they come back. Two: check the iron line on the Day 33 label photo (~27 mg), cook one iron meal this week (red meat, or lentils and beans, with something vitamin-C rich on the plate), and move her tea or coffee at least an hour away from the vitamin. If she is vegetarian or vegan, or has had anaemia or heavy periods before, add to question ten: should she start extra iron now?
